title: Initial GET can create duplicate singleton config rows under concurrency
reasoning: GET /config performs a read-then-insert singleton creation path. On a fresh database, two concurrent authenticated GETs can both observe no row, then each insert and commit a default ClientConfig. Subsequent calls use select(...).first() with no deterministic singleton key or ordering in this helper, so the app can read one arbitrary row while another row remains stale, violating the singleton configuration contract.
reproduction: On an empty client_config table, issue two concurrent GET /api/config requests using separate database sessions. Both can pass the config is None branch before either commit completes, leaving more than one ClientConfig row.
recommendation: Make the singleton explicit and atomic: use a fixed primary key or unique singleton column plus an insert-or-ignore/upsert pattern, handle integrity conflicts by re-selecting the row, and avoid unordered first() for singleton reads.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the existing config tests call the endpoint serially after clearing the table. They do not exercise concurrent first access or assert that only one client_config row exists after GET.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that clears client_config, invokes get_or_create_config concurrently with separate sessions, and asserts only one row exists and all callers receive the same row.
minimumFixScope: get_or_create_config plus the ClientConfig schema/migration if a fixed singleton key or unique constraint is introduced.
